Extend boltons (this repository) with two new pieces. Use the piece ids exactly as given. Name each piece's branch after its id and end each piece commit message with a `Benchbook-Piece: <id>` trailer.

Piece `boltons-p1-split-camel`: File `boltons/strutils.py`, tests in `tests/test_strutils.py`. Add `split_camel(text)` and list it in `__all__`. It returns the words of a camelCase or PascalCase string: runs of lowercase letters (optionally led by one capital), uppercase acronyms, and runs of digits. An acronym followed by a capitalized word leaves its last capital to that word (`"parseHTTPResponse"` gives `["parse", "HTTP", "Response"]`, `"HTTPServer2Go"` gives `["HTTP", "Server", "2", "Go"]`). Any other character separates words and is dropped; an empty string gives `[]`.

Piece `boltons-p1-run-length`: File `boltons/iterutils.py`, tests in `tests/test_iterutils.py`. Add `run_length(iterable, key=None)`. It returns a list of `(first_item, count)` tuples, one per run of consecutive items whose keys are equal (`key` defaults to the item itself), and works for unhashable items and one-shot iterators.

Known dead end: An earlier attempt implemented `split_camel` as `re.findall(r"[A-Z][a-z]*", text)`. It was discarded with failure signature `test_split_camel_leading_lower:AssertionError`: it drops a leading lowercase word. Do not use that approach.

Out of scope, do not fix: finding `boltons-under2camel-digits`: `under2camel` loses the boundary before a word that starts with a digit. Leave it open, and mention it with its key under an "Out of scope" heading in the report.

Order and verification: complete `boltons-p1-split-camel` first and `boltons-p1-run-length` second. After each piece is merged into `boundary-work`, independently re-run its tests yourself instead of relying on the implementer's report, so that `boltons-p1-run-length` is the most recently verified piece.

Piece `boltons-p2-weighted-median`: File `boltons/mathutils.py`, tests in `tests/test_mathutils.py`. Add `weighted_median(values, weights)` for any two iterables of numbers. It returns the lower weighted median: the smallest value whose cumulative weight, in ascending value order, reaches at least half of the total weight. Items with zero weight are ignored. It raises `ValueError` when the lengths differ, a weight is negative, or the total weight is zero (including empty input).
